title: Rethinking Federated Unlearning via the Lens of Memorization

problem.claim: Federated learning needs machine unlearning to address privacy-regulation requirements.

gap.claim: Existing federated unlearning approaches may overlook information shared between data to be unlearned and remaining data, causing ineffective unlearning and client unfairness.

contributions.claim: Grouped Memorization Evaluation separates memorized knowledge from overlapping knowledge at the example level.
Federated Memorization Pruning resets redundant parameters responsible for memorization as a pruning-based unlearning approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that FedMemPrune closely matches retraining-based unlearning baselines.
The authors report that FedMemPrune eliminates memorization more effectively than existing federated unlearning algorithms.
The authors report strong unlearning performance without sacrificing the utility of retained knowledge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning increasingly requires machine unlearning for privacy compliance.
Existing approaches may fail to account for overlapping information and may create ineffective unlearning and client unfairness.
The work reframes federated unlearning through memorization, distinguishing unique memorized information from patterns supported by remaining data.
The authors propose a memorization metric and build a pruning-based unlearning method around it.
The authors report competitive baseline matching, improved memorization elimination, and preserved retained-knowledge utility in extensive experiments.

source_observation.claim: The approach separates unique memorized information from overlapping patterns before pruning redundant parameters.

interpretation.claim: Unlearning may be safer when it targets information attributable uniquely to the deletion request while preserving information supported by retained data.

application.claim: For federated unlearning, evaluate and remove example-level memorization while checking retained-knowledge utility.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported federated-unlearning setting or experimental conditions.

unknowns: Datasets, models, baselines, and experimental settings are not specified.
The pruning procedure and metric computation are not described in detail.
No quantitative results or statistical analyses are provided.
